context.before: Fernway is building Insights, a feature that explains why support tickets spike. The beta build is ready, but scope, price and the launch plan were still open.
context.call: Emma ran the weekly sync. Laura walked through what a support manager sees, then Daniel and Sarah argued two ways to price it.
context.question: What does Insights do at launch, how do we price it, and what is the launch plan?
context.decided: Beta on 23 Nov with five steps only. Test both prices for two weeks. Launch in three weeks, with a gate before each step.

summary.lead: Ship Insights small, price it with evidence.
summary.accent: The beta opens on 23 Nov with five steps only. Both prices get tested for two weeks before anyone chooses.

chapters.title: What this meeting must decide
see: Beta date depends on the Zendesk connector
Three big accounts already asked for Insights
chapters.summary: Emma sets the three things to decide. The only blocker for the beta is the Zendesk connector: if it is ready by 20 Nov, the beta opens on 23 Nov. Three big accounts already asked for Insights.

quotes.text: Beta opens on the twenty-third, as long as the connector is green on the twentieth.

chapters.title: What Insights does for a support manager
see: Five steps: connect, spot, explain, suggest, report
Explaining why is the hard part
chapters.summary: Laura walks through a support manager's Monday: connect, spot the spike, explain why, suggest a fix, send a Friday report. Marco says explaining why is the hard part. Emma locks version 1 to these five steps.

quotes.text: So the promise is, from tickets went up, to here's why and what to do, on one screen.

chapters.onscreen: Laura's prototype of the five steps.

chapters.title: What customers plug in, and trust
see: Ticket history, release notes, customer list
Upload screen for messy release notes
SOC 2 report and a data note
chapters.summary: For the explain step, customers plug in ticket history, release notes and their customer list. Release notes are messy, so Laura will design an upload screen. Security needs the SOC 2 report and a data note. Sample-data mode waits for version 2.

quotes.text: About half our customers keep them in Google Docs, not in Jira.

chapters.title: Pricing: starter tier or usage add-on?
chapters.summary: Daniel wants a $29 starter tier for small teams. Sarah wants an add-on priced per 1,000 tickets, because cheap tiers pulled revenue down last year. Laura suggests testing both, and Emma agrees.

quotes.text: You both want the same thing. More paying teams without hurting margin.
So what if we test both? Half the beta trials see the starter tier, half see the add-on.

chapters.title: How the price test works, and what's open
chapters.summary: A price wins if it beats today's 14% trial conversion without lowering revenue per account. Sarah and Olivia set up both price pages by 18 Nov. Free access for existing customers, and who answers AI questions on sales calls, are still open.

quotes.text: So a price wins if it beats fourteen percent without lowering revenue per account.

chapters.title: The three-week launch plan
see: Week 1 beta, week 2 launch, week 3 review
chapters.summary: Three weeks: beta, public launch with Tom's agency, then review the numbers and pick the price. Each step has a gate: no critical bugs before week 2, six of ten customers using it weekly before week 3.

quotes.text: Gate before week three. At least six of the ten beta customers use it every week.

chapters.title: What we measure, and recap
chapters.summary: Four numbers to track. Time saved needs a baseline, so Laura adds a question to the onboarding calls. Emma recaps.

quotes.text: Recap. Beta on the twenty-third. Five steps only. A two-week price test.

decisions.text: The beta opens on 23 Nov, if the connector is green on 20 Nov.
decisions.why: The Zendesk connector is the only thing blocking the beta.

decisions.text: Version 1 is five steps. No custom dashboards.
decisions.why: Custom dashboards would add a month.

decisions.text: Test both prices on beta trials for two weeks.
decisions.why: Sales and Finance want the same outcome, and nobody knows which price gets there.

decisions.text: A price wins if it beats 14% trial conversion without lowering revenue per account.
decisions.why: Agreed before the test, so the result can't be argued later.

decisions.text: Launch in three weeks, with a gate before each step.
decisions.why: Each step only starts when the previous one proves itself.

decisions.text: Track weekly active teams, tickets explained, conversion and time saved.
decisions.why: These show whether Insights is used and worth paying for.
